reason: While some regular people in this passage are portrayed positively or neutrally—such as the young women drawing water who helpfully provide directions, the servant who makes a practical suggestion to consult Samuel, and the general populace who accept Saul as king—the text explicitly includes a negative characterization of a group called 'benei beliya'al' (בְנֵי בְלִיַּעַל, literally 'sons of worthlessness'). These individuals despise Saul and refuse to bring him gifts, representing an unfavorable portrayal. The passage thus shows mixed portrayals of regular people rather than a uniformly favorable one.
